Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 32, verse 2:

﴿The revelation of the Book﴾ means the Qur'an. ﴿There is no doubt in it﴾ means there is no doubt that it is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The negation of doubt is with respect to the belief of the people of truth and with respect to what the matter actually is in itself, not with respect to the belief of the people of falsehood. ﴿From the Lord of the worlds﴾ is connected to "revelation."

**[Ibn Juzayy, *al-Tashil*, on Surah 32, verse 3]**

﴿Or do they say...﴾ The pronoun refers to Quraysh, and *am* (﴿أَمْ﴾) means *bal* ("rather"). The hamza ﴿لِتُنذِرَ﴾ is connected to what precedes it, or to an implied element: ﴿so that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you﴾. The phrase ﴿مَّآ أَتَاهُم مِّن نَّذِيرٍ﴾ means: from *al-fatra* (the interval between prophets) since the time of Jesus. Messengers had come before that, such as Abraham and others. When the interval lengthened for these people, God sent a messenger to warn them, in order to establish the proof against them.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 32, verse 4:

﴿Istawā ʿalā al-ʿarsh﴾ (He established Himself upon the Throne). This has been mentioned in al-Aʿraf [7:53].

﴿Mā lakum min dūnihi min waliyyin wa lā shafīʿ﴾ (You have no protector or intercessor besides Him). The negation of intercession is of two kinds. The first is intercession for the disbelievers, which does not exist at all, absolutely. The second is that intercession for the believers occurs only by Allah's permission, as in His saying: ﴿Mā min shafīʿin illā min baʿdi idhnihi﴾ (There is no intercessor except after His permission) [Yunus 10:3].

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 32, verse 5:

﴿He arranges the affair﴾: i.e., He is the one who manages all affairs. It was also said: the affair commanded, meaning acts of obedience, but the first (opinion) is more sound. ﴿From the heaven to the earth﴾: i.e., He sends down what He has arranged and decreed from the heaven to the earth. ﴿Then it ascends to Him in a day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: the meaning is that Allah executes what He has decreed from the heaven to the earth, then the report of that ascends to Him in a day of the days of this world, whose measure, if it were traversed at the ordinary pace of humans, would be a thousand years, because the distance between the heaven and the earth is five hundred years. So the thousand (years) is the (total) of the descent of the command to the earth and its ascent to the heaven. It was also said: Allah casts to the angels matters of a thousand years of human years, and that is one day of Allah's days; when it is finished, He casts to them the like of it. So the meaning is that affairs are executed in His sight during this period, and then they return to Him in the end, because the outcome of affairs belongs to Him. Thus the ascent, in this view, is an expression for the affairs' return to Him.
﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾. The unseen (al-ghayb) is what is hidden from created beings, and the witnessed (al-shahada) is what they have witnessed.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 32, verse 7:

﴿He perfected everything He created﴾. That is, He made all creatures excellent and well-formed. It is also read with the lam sukūn (خَلْقَهُ read as "khalqahu" with the lam pronounced as a sukūn), as a substitution (badal). ﴿And He began the creation of man from clay﴾. He means Adam, peace be upon him.

﴿nasluhu﴾ meaning his offspring, ﴿min sulalatin min ma'in maheen﴾ meaning from an extract of a base fluid, that is, the semen. Al-sulala (extract) is derived from sall, yasillu (to draw out), as if the water is drawn out of the human being. Al-maheen means weak.

﴿Then He proportioned him﴾, meaning He made him upright (qawwamahu). ﴿And breathed into him of His Spirit﴾ is an expression for bringing life into being within him. The Spirit is attributed to Allah by an attribution of ownership (idafat mulk, meaning a possessive construction, like "the house of Zayd" or "the camel of Allah"), and it may also be intended as an attribution of distinction (ikhtisas, meaning singling out and honoring), because the reality (kunh) of the Spirit is known only to Allah.

*"Is it that when we are lost in the earth..."* That is, when we perish and become dust.

The meaning of this statement, as reported from the disbelievers, is the denial of resurrection as something unlikely. The governing element (al-'amil) of إذا ('idha, "when") is the sense of their words, *"Indeed we are in a new creation"*, and its implied meaning is: "we will be resurrected."

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 32, verse 11:

﴿The Angel of Death, who has been charged with you, will take your souls﴾ His name is ʿAzrāʾīl (ʿAzrāʾīl), and under his command are angels.

**Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 32, verse 12:**

﴿وَلَوْ تَرَىٰ﴾ may be that *law* (lau, "if") is for wishing (*tamanni*), and its interpretation with regard to God is like the interpretation of hoping (*tarajji*), which has been mentioned. Or it may be for negation (*imtina'*), where the answer (*jawab*) is omitted, and its implied meaning is: "And if you could see the condition of the criminals in the Hereafter, you would see a dreadful matter." ﴿نَاكِسُواْ رُءُوسِهِمْ﴾ is an expression for humiliation, grief and regret. ﴿رَبَّنَآ أَبْصَرْنَا وَسَمِعْنَا﴾ its implied meaning: they say, "Our Lord, we have now seen and heard the realities."

"And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance." It means that if He had willed to guide all creatures, He would have done so, for He is capable of that: by placing faith in their hearts and warding off from them Satan and desires. But He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 32, verse 14:

﴿So taste [it] for what you forgot﴾. That is, it is said to them: "Taste," and forgetting here means abandoning.

﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, that is, they rise up. The meaning is that they leave their beds at night because of their many voluntary prayers (nawafil, prayers beyond those obligatory). Whoever prays the 'Isha' and the Subh (Fajr) prayers in congregation has taken his share of this.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 32, verse 17:

﴿So no soul knows what is hidden for them of the delight of the eyes﴾ Meaning: no one knows the measure of the bounty God gives them. Hamzah recited ﴿ukhfi﴾ with a sukun on the yā' (ي), so that it is the verb of the Speaker, who is God, exalted is He.
﴿Is then one who is a believer﴾, the verse. He means the believers and the defiantly disobedient in general. It was also said that he means Ali ibn Abi Talib and Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt.

﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.﴾ The phrase "which" refers to the punishment, which has been described, and for this reason the pronoun mentioned in His words ﴿which you used to deny﴾ returns to it. If it is asked: why is the punishment described here and the pronoun returned to it, while in Saba' the Fire is described and the pronoun returns to it, and He says "the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny"? The answer has three aspects. The first is that in the prostration chapter (al-Sajdah) the punishment is singled out for description, out of concern for it, since its mention has been repeated in His words ﴿And We will surely let them taste from the nearer punishment, short of the greater punishment﴾. The second is that in the prostration chapter the mention of the Fire came first, so the original arrangement was that it should be mentioned afterwards by a pronoun (damir). However, the apparent noun (al-zahir) was put in place of the pronoun (al-mudmar). Just as a pronoun is not described, what takes its place, which is the Fire, is not described either. Thus the punishment was described and the Fire was not described. The third, which is the strongest, is that describing the Fire was ruled out in the prostration chapter, so the punishment was described instead. Describing it was ruled out because it had already been mentioned. When you mention a thing and then repeat its mention, it is not permissible to describe it, as in your saying: "I saw a man, so I honoured the man." It is not permissible to describe him, lest it be understood that he is someone else.

﴿And We will surely let them taste from the nearer punishment, short of the greater punishment﴾. It means hunger and the calamities of this world. It is also said: the killing on the day of Badr. It is also said: the punishment of the grave. This last view is far-fetched because of His words ﴿so that perhaps they will return﴾.

Verse 32:22 (the meaning): "Indeed, We will take retribution against the criminals."

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on this verse:

This is a warning for those who are reminded of the signs of their Lord and then turn away from them. The original wording would have been: "Indeed, We will take retribution against them" (inna minhu muntaqimun). However, He placed "the criminals" (al-mujrimin) in the position of the pronoun in order to describe them as characterized by criminality (al-ijram). He also placed the prepositional phrase before "muntaqimun" (retribution-takers) for emphasis (al-mubalagha).

﴿So be not in doubt about meeting him.﴾ [Al-Mirya] is doubt (shakk), and the pronoun refers to Musa. That is: do not doubt your meeting with Musa on the night of the Isra'. It was also said: the meaning is, do not doubt the meeting with Musa and the Book that was revealed to him. On this reading, the Book is the Torah. It was also said: the Book here is a generic noun (jins), and the meaning is: We gave Musa the Book, so do not you doubt your meeting with the Book that was revealed to you. He used "meeting" (al-liqa') to express the sending down of the Book, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed, you receive the Qur'an﴾ [An-Naml: 6].
﴿Yafṣilu baynahum﴾ (He will judge between them). The pronoun refers to all of creation. It is said that it refers specifically to the Children of Israel.

**Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on Surah 32, verse 26:**

﴿Has it not been made clear to them?﴾ This was mentioned in Ta-Ha [128]. ﴿...as they walk through their dwellings.﴾ The pronoun in *yamshuna* (they walk) refers to the people of Makkah, meaning: they walk through the dwellings of the people who were destroyed, like His saying: ﴿And it has become clear to you from their dwellings﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 38]. It has also been said that the pronoun refers to those who were destroyed, meaning: We destroyed them while they were walking in their dwellings. The first view is better, because it contains a proof against the people of Makkah.

Translation:

﴿the barren land﴾: meaning the land in which there is no vegetation at all, because of its extreme thirst.

[When will this victory be?] Meaning: the judgment between the Muslims and the disbelievers in the Hereafter. It was also said that it means the conquest of Makkah, but this is far-fetched because of His saying: [Say: On the Day of Victory, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them]. That refers to the Hereafter. It was also said that it means the conquest of Makkah, because whoever believed on the day of the conquest of Makkah, his faith benefited him.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 32, verse 30:

﴿So turn away from them﴾ [is] abrogated by the sword (naskh, abrogation: the replacement or cancellation of a ruling by a later one). ﴿And wait, for they too are waiting﴾. That is: wait for their destruction, for they are waiting for your destruction. In this there is a warning (tahdid) to them.
